knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(magrittr)
include.code = TRUE

1 Questão 1

  1. Examine a variável dependente. Necessita de alguma transformação? Por que?

  2. Faça o gráfico da variável \(y\) contra a variável \(x\). Proponha uma possível forma funcional.

  3. Teste um modelo de relação linear. Como ficou o ajustamento? Que gráficos você pode fazer?

  4. Você proporia algum modelo diferente da relação linear? Se sim, teste.

set.seed(10)
x = rnorm(250, 4, 1)
y = 150*x - 20.5*x^2 +8800 + 40*rnorm(x)
x = x %>% round(1)
y = y %>% round(1)
data.q1 = data.frame(y, x)
plot(x, y, pch = 20, col = "gray")

mhist(y)

mhist(y %>% log)

m = lm(y~x)
library(lmtest)
## Loading required package: zoo
## 
## Attaching package: 'zoo'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     as.Date, as.Date.numeric
reset(m)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  m
## RESET = 31.63, df1 = 2, df2 = 246, p-value = 5.961e-13
shapiro.test(m$residuals %>% scale)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  m$residuals %>% scale
## W = 0.99193, p-value = 0.1879
mhist(m$residuals %>% scale)

plot(x, y, pch = 20, col = "gray")
abline(m, col = "blue")

m2 = lm(y~x+I(x^2))
reset(m2)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  m2
## RESET = 0.16152, df1 = 2, df2 = 245, p-value = 0.8509
shapiro.test(m2$residuals %>% scale)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  m2$residuals %>% scale
## W = 0.99586, p-value = 0.7466
mhist(m2$residuals %>% scale)

plot(x, y, pch = 20, col = "gray")
.x = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100)
.y = predict(m2, data.frame(x = .x))
lines(.x, .y, col = "blue")

2 Questão 2

No modelo proposto, a variável y é explicada por x. Espera-se uma relação de grau mais elevado. Monte o percurso investigativo e explique cada etapa.

set.seed(10)
x = rnorm(250, 3, 1)
y = 4.4*x^3+ 20*x - 32.5*x^2 +8800 + 30*rnorm(x)
x = x %>% round(1)
y = y %>% round(1)
data.q2 = data.frame(y, x)
plot(x, y, pch = 20, col = "gray")

mhist(y)

mhist(y %>% log)

3 Questão 3

No modelo proposto, a variável y é explicada por X1, X2 e X3. Espera-se relações de segundo ou terceiro grau para as variáveis independentes. Monte o percurso investigativo e explique cada etapa.

set.seed(10)
x = MASS::mvrnorm(250, c(10, 10, 10), diag(c(1, 2, 1.5)))
y = 10+3*rnorm(x[,1])+x%*%matrix(c(-1, 2, 3), ncol = 1)-0.5*x[,2]^2
x = x %>% round(1) + 0.1
y = y %>% as.numeric %>% round(1)
data = data.frame(y, x)
data.q3 = data
plot(x[,2], y, pch = 20, col = "gray")

mhist(y)

m = lm(y~., data)
library(lmtest)
reset(m)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  m
## RESET = 17.101, df1 = 2, df2 = 244, p-value = 1.121e-07

##

## data:  m$residuals %>% scale
## W = 0.9915, p-value = 0.1568
mhist(m$residuals %>% scale)

summary(m)

4 Questão 4

No modelo proposto, a variável y é explicada por X1, X2 e X3. Espera-se coeficientes positivos para X1 e X2 e investiga-se uma possível relacão de moderação de X2 para o efeito de X1. Monte o percurso investigativo e explique cada etapa.

set.seed(10)
x = MASS::mvrnorm(250, c(10, 10, 10), diag(c(1, 2, 1.5)))
y = 3*x[,1]+2*x[,2]-4*x[,1]*x[,2]+rnorm(x[,1])+600
x = x %>% round(1) + 0.1
y = y %>% as.numeric %>% round(1)
data = data.frame(y, x)
data.q4 = data
plot(x[,2], y, pch = 20, col = "gray")

mhist(y)

m = lm(y~X1+X2+X3+X1:X2, data)
library(lmtest)
reset(m)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  m
## RESET = 0.27176, df1 = 2, df2 = 243, p-value = 0.7623
shapiro.test(m$residuals %>% scale)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test

## data:  m$residuals %>% scale
## W = 0.99472, p-value = 0.5408
mhist(m$residuals %>% scale)

summary(m)

5 Questão 5

Na busca por um efeito de cointegração examinou-se duas séries temporais.

Explique os resultados dos exames determinando 1) se um modelo VECM para esses dados é adequado, e porque. 2) Se o VECM for adequado, qual é a série que comanda o sistema?

library(tseries)
## Registered S3 method overwritten by 'quantmod':
##   method            from
##   as.zoo.data.frame zoo
set.seed(3)
err = arima.sim(model = list(order = c(1, 0, 0), ar = 0.68), 200)
#err=rnorm(200)
x = rnorm(err)
xcum = cumsum(x)+5
ycum = xcum+1*err+3
lm(ycum~xcum) %>% residuals -> res
plot.ts(data.frame(xcum, ycum, res), plot.type = "single", col = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen")); abline(h=0, col = "gray")

acf(xcum); acf(ycum); acf(res)

pacf(xcum); pacf(ycum); pacf(res)

tseries::adf.test(xcum)
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  xcum
## Dickey-Fuller = -2.9581, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.1748
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
tseries::adf.test(ycum)
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  ycum
## Dickey-Fuller = -2.5143, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.3607
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
tseries::adf.test(res)
## Warning in tseries::adf.test(res): p-value smaller than printed p-value
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  res
## Dickey-Fuller = -4.098, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
tseries::adf.test(xcum %>% diff)
## Warning in tseries::adf.test(xcum %>% diff): p-value smaller than printed
## p-value
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  xcum %>% diff
## Dickey-Fuller = -4.9585, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
tseries::adf.test(ycum %>% diff)
## Warning in tseries::adf.test(ycum %>% diff): p-value smaller than printed
## p-value
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  ycum %>% diff
## Dickey-Fuller = -5.7188, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
acf(xcum %>% diff); acf(ycum %>% diff)

pacf(xcum %>% diff); pacf(ycum %>% diff)

library(urca)
ca.jo(data.frame(ycum, xcum)) -> vecm; vecm %>% summary

6 Questão 6

Um modelo de dados em painel (Empresa x Ano) foi estudado.

Explique os resultados obtidos e qual o modelo mais adequado.

set.seed(12)
Empresa = 1:10
ano = 2000:2024
x = MASS::mvrnorm(250, c(0, 0, 0), diag(rep(1, 3))) %>% matrix(ncol = 3)
y = rep(Empresa, each = 25)/10+rep(ano, times = 10)/200000+(0.1*c(1, 0, -3)%*%t(x))+rnorm(250)
y = as.numeric(y)
data = data.frame(E = rep(Empresa, each = 25), A = rep(ano, times = 10), y = y, x)
pdata = plm::pdata.frame(data, index = c("E", "A"))
m.pooled = plm::plm(y~X1+X2+X3, pdata, model = "pooling")
summary(m.pooled)
## Pooling Model
## 
## Call:
## plm::plm(formula = y ~ X1 + X2 + X3, data = pdata, model = "pooling")
## 
## Balanced Panel: n = 10, T = 25, N = 250
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min.   1st Qu.    Median   3rd Qu.      Max. 
## -3.239984 -0.677900 -0.043131  0.638731  2.866649 
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error t-value  Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.603188   0.065202  9.2510 < 2.2e-16 ***
## X1           0.175788   0.068210  2.5771   0.01055 *  
## X2          -0.152318   0.068273 -2.2310   0.02658 *  
## X3          -0.287552   0.069636 -4.1293 4.987e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Total Sum of Squares:    285.12
## Residual Sum of Squares: 258.13
## R-Squared:      0.094677
## Adj. R-Squared: 0.083636
## F-statistic: 8.57537 on 3 and 246 DF, p-value: 1.948e-05
m.within = plm::plm(y~X1+X2+X3, pdata, model = "within")
summary(m.within)
## Oneway (individual) effect Within Model
## 
## Call:
## plm::plm(formula = y ~ X1 + X2 + X3, data = pdata, model = "within")
## 
## Balanced Panel: n = 10, T = 25, N = 250
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min.   1st Qu.    Median   3rd Qu.      Max. 
## -2.939840 -0.679419  0.016906  0.552601  2.632928 
## 
## Coefficients:
##     Estimate Std. Error t-value  Pr(>|t|)    
## X1  0.149795   0.066763  2.2437   0.02578 *  
## X2 -0.158250   0.064742 -2.4443   0.01524 *  
## X3 -0.296155   0.066435 -4.4578 1.278e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Total Sum of Squares:    249.17
## Residual Sum of Squares: 222.98
## R-Squared:      0.10513
## Adj. R-Squared: 0.059819
## F-statistic: 9.2809 on 3 and 237 DF, p-value: 7.9408e-06
plm::fixef(m.within)
##         1         2         3         4         5         6         7         8 
## -0.053685  0.299248  0.392575  0.595007  0.271239  0.957576  0.661772  0.633862 
##         9        10 
##  0.941660  1.303466
plm::pFtest(m.within, m.pooled)
## 
##  F test for individual effects
## 
## data:  y ~ X1 + X2 + X3
## F = 4.1517, df1 = 9, df2 = 237, p-value = 5.491e-05
## alternative hypothesis: significant effects
m.random = plm::plm(y~X1+X2+X3, pdata, model = "random")
summary(m.random)
## Oneway (individual) effect Random Effect Model 
##    (Swamy-Arora's transformation)
## 
## Call:
## plm::plm(formula = y ~ X1 + X2 + X3, data = pdata, model = "random")
## 
## Balanced Panel: n = 10, T = 25, N = 250
## 
## Effects:
##                  var std.dev share
## idiosyncratic 0.9408  0.9700  0.85
## individual    0.1654  0.4067  0.15
## theta: 0.5695
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min.   1st Qu.    Median   3rd Qu.      Max. 
## -3.076003 -0.669524 -0.047828  0.536512  2.678198 
## 
## Coefficients:

plm::ranef(m.random)

plm::phtest(m.random, m.within)
